risk_based_sizing._note: Van Tharp / Elder / Turtle framework (research 2026-07-16, user-approved). Every BUY risks at most risk_per_trade_pct of equity measured entry-to-stop; the validator CLAMPS oversized proposals down to the risk budget rather than rejecting. Portfolio heat = sum over open positions of entry-basis committed risk max(0,(avg_cost-stop)*qty)/equity; new BUYs are rejected past portfolio_heat_cap_pct (user chose 8%; literature 6-10%). Theme cap: committed initial risk sharing one demand_driver <= theme_initial_risk_cap_pct. Entry-basis heat means trailed stops above cost free the budget (pyramiding into winners stays possible). momentum_unwind_risk_scale halves the risk budget when momentum_health flags an unwind.

scale_in._note: Adds allowed only into winners (price above blended cost, never averaging down), max 2 adds, combined exposure stays inside the per-name cap. Partial exits via sell_fraction in (0,1].

conviction_tier._note: When earned, conviction raises the RISK budget to 1.5% (and the notional ceilings accordingly); base tier stays 1%.

position_sizing._fractional_stop_note: CONSEQUENCE OF THE $1,000 BOOK, measured 2026-07-21 against the live 187-name universe. Alpaca carries fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, so a GTC stop needs a whole-share leg (execution/alpaca_broker.py, MIN_WHOLE_SHARES_FOR_LIMIT=4 and _resting stop arming). At a $1,429 position (the $10,000 book) 69.5% of the universe got a full exchange-held GTC stop attached at entry and only 2.1% fell under one share. At a $143 position (this book) those become 3.2% and 72.2%: most entries are now sub-one-share, so their protective stop is a DAY order that expires at the close and is re-armed by scripts/stop_watch.py on the Actions cron. Intraday protection is a real resting broker order and is essentially unchanged; what is lost is the overnight/weekend leg, where the exit now depends on the poller's next tick rather than the opening print. Accepted deliberately: the gap risk is real but denominated in single-digit dollars at this size. Do NOT read a low whole-share count as a reason to skip a setup.

quality._claim_grounding_note: Added 2026-07-25, DEFAULT OFF pending evidence, same staged rollout as _tradeability_note below. WHAT IT DOES: validator._check_claim_grounding greps every entity a BUY's variant_perception/catalysts name against the FULL context bundle and rejects the ones that appear nowhere in it. Built from four real incidents the LLM risk desk caught by hand: DDOG 07-22 ('JMP Securities raised its target to $311' - the string 'JMP' appears ZERO times in that day's bundle), MELI 07-24 ('Loggi acquisition', a Citi fair-value cut, '14 new Brazil fulfillment centers'), IBKR 07-22 (an invented 'fourth consecutive beat' with an EMPTY guidance_ledger), UNP 07-24 (a 'binding MOU signed one day earlier' that inverts the actual sequence). WHY IT IS NOT ON YET: CLAUDE.md step 5 makes WebSearch MANDATORY before any BUY, so the brain is REQUIRED to bring in facts that legitimately are not in the bundle - blocking on 'absent from bundle' would reject true WebSearch findings alongside fabricated ones, and a false rejection costs a real trade on a book that has already gone days without one. Until proposals carry per-claim sources, the SAME computation is fed to the risk desk every run (validator.unsourced_claims -> runlib.brain_io), which can weigh the WebSearch context a regex cannot. TO ENABLE: watch the risk-desk prompt's UNSOURCED CLAIMS block for a week; if the entities it lists are consistently real fabrications rather than WebSearch-sourced truth, flip this to true. Precision was tuned against the 7 real BUY proposals in journal/proposals + journal/rejected: multi-word candidates are only taken from an explicit attribution pattern ('<Firm> raised/said/cut'), because the bare proper-noun pass produced prose fragments like 'MINIMUM CONTRACTED' and 'Case After Strong' that no bundle would ever contain verbatim.

The remainder may be ADDED only after a completed session close confirms, on a later slot (normal add-on rules: above blended cost, max 2 adds). Starters do NOT consume a calibration_probe slot. Every other cap applies: max 2 new positions/day, 20% min cash, $200/20% max position, 8% heat, theme caps. validator._check_starter.

calibration_probe._note: ADDED 2026-08-05. A BUY scored honestly in [0.50, 0.60) is no longer rejected outright: it trades as a CALIBRATION PROBE at risk_scale x the normal risk budget (0.5% of equity instead of 1%), stamped calibration_probe on the proposal AND persisted onto the position's plan at fill, with at most max_open_probes such positions on the book at once (validator._check_probe_limits). WHY: the hard 0.60 floor could never learn whether 0.50-0.60 setups win, because it never let one trade - HPE on 2026-08-05 died at 0.57 the same afternoon a validated DXCM entry died on a keyword false-positive, on a book that had made 3 trades in a month - and its only lasting lesson to the proposer was that honesty costs the trade while writing 0.62 sails through. The desk's confidence haircut (max -0.10) previously turned into a death sentence whenever it landed under 0.60; now it converts the trade to half-risk instead, so the desk can express skepticism without killing the setup. Probe fills grade into their own 0.50-0.60 bucket (tools/performance_breakdown._confidence_bucket), so once 5+ close the existing calibration machinery has REAL fill data: if the bucket proves losing (<40% WR) the losing-bucket gate starts rejecting it with evidence, and if it proves fine that argues the floor down. Every other gate - RR>=2, geometry, volatility stop, heat, theme caps, earnings window, risk desk - applies to a probe at full strength; below probe min_confidence remains a hard rejection.

earnings_window._note: ADDED 2026-08-03. Until now there was NO coded earnings rule anywhere - `days_to_earnings` appeared ZERO times in validator.py - so 'trade around the binary' was entirely the brain's judgment applied against a 45-day default horizon. In earnings season that excludes essentially the whole universe, and it did: across 2026-07-13..08-03 run after run passed on every candidate for a print somewhere inside the swing window (08-03 alone rejected MPC and AMGN for an 08-04 print, then NET and TEAM for 08-06, and traded nothing). The gate is now NARROW and the narrowness is the point: only a print within pre_print_blackout_days blocks a BUY, everything outside it is explicitly tradeable, and a name that has ALREADY reported within post_print_drift_days is a PREFERRED lane (the binary is resolved and the geometry is clean). allow_trade_through_with_case lets the brain trade the print deliberately when the binary IS the thesis, by supplying an `earnings_case` of >= min_earnings_case_chars. Fail-open: a ticker the committed calendar does not carry is NOT MEASURED, never 'no print'.

quality._min_rr_note: Raised 1.0 -> 2.0 (2026-07-16, user-approved after expectancy research): breakeven win rate at 2:1 is 33%, keeping the book profitable across the realistic 40-55% band; a 1:1 floor loses money below ~52% wins after costs (Minervini/O'Neil both demand ~2:1 at entry).
quality._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.
quality._trailing_stop_note: Chandelier exit (LeBeau/Elder; user-approved 2026-07-16): once a position's high-water mark puts (high_water - 3xATR) ABOVE the plan stop, the effective stop ratchets up with it - never down, never widened, and deliberately NO breakeven jump at +1R (research shows early breakeven moves gut trend expectancy). Forced exits fire on the effective stop; reason trailing_stop_breached when the trail was binding.
quality._falsifiability_note: ADDED 2026-07-19 (audit). variant_perception, scenarios and thesis_invalidators were PRESENCE-checked only, while CLAUDE.md twice called variant_perception 'validator-enforced' - a single non-space character satisfied it. min_invalidator_chars was 12, so 'drops below 50dma' (17) passed as a binding falsifier. scenarios' probabilities need not have summed to 1, and tools/scenario_ev.py computed honest EV whose only callers were two RENDERING paths. Now: invalidating_print needs a numeric threshold, time_box needs a date or day-count, variant_perception needs a figure and a dated resolution, and scenario probabilities must sum to ~1 with a non-negative probability-weighted return. These check SHAPE, not argument quality - no regex grades a thesis, and the risk desk and the reader remain the judges of that.

theme_risk._note: Market value of positions sharing the same demand_driver plus proposed size must stay under this fraction of equity. Catches DELL+HPE style single-factor books that sector caps miss when names sit in different GICS sleeves. Fail-open if demand_driver missing (field check already rejects). The notional cap here complements the RISK-based theme cap in position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.theme_initial_risk_cap_pct.

regime_gate._note: Coded regime filter (Faber 2007/2013: ~halved max drawdown over a century; user-approved 2026-07-16). When the benchmark trend is hostile (SPY below its 200DMA), new BUYs are REJECTED (regime_gate_spy_below_200dma) - exits and holds are never blocked, and existing stops keep working, consistent with the evidence that the filter's value is blocking NEW risk, not forced liquidation. Momentum-unwind detection (tools/momentum_health.py) separately halves the risk budget via position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.momentum_unwind_risk_scale rather than hard-blocking. Fail-open when regime data is absent from market_context.

book_risk._unknown_beta_note: ADDED 2026-08-03. The beta ceiling used to reject outright whenever ANY name in the projected book lacked a beta in the correlation feed, and on 2026-07-28 that killed a BKR BUY whose only unknown name was BKR itself against a 100%-CASH book - a $49 position on a $984 book cannot make anything a leveraged index bet, and the same trade was re-proposed and filled hours later. Failing closed on an unmeasurable input is right when the input could hide real exposure; it is wrong when the worst case is computable. Unknown betas on the PROPOSED name are now assumed to be this value (deliberately pessimistic - the ceiling itself) and the cap is enforced against that. HELD positions missing a beta still fail closed: an exposure already carried cannot be bounded by sizing, and only the one being added can.
book_risk._tradeability_note: Added 2026-07-19, both DEFAULT OFF pending evidence. Both floors currently fail OPEN on missing data: a proposal on a ticker absent from market_context skips the stop noise-band check entirely (a 1% stop on an 8%-ATR name passes), and a name with no market-cap figure clears the $1B floor by default. The enforcement is built and tested; enabling is a one-line flip once the evidence is in. require_volatility_data: a live gather covers 182/187 tickers with ZERO universe names absent, so the coverage case is already strong - held off only because 26 existing tests pass market_context={} and rewriting that many safety fixtures hours before going live is how a real assertion gets weakened by accident. Enable after a week of runs, then fix the fixtures deliberately. require_market_cap_data: weaker case and it stays off longer. market_cap_usd is NOT a bundle field (0% coverage there); orchestrator.py resolves it PER PROPOSAL from deep_fundamentals, then scan rows, then a LIVE lookup - so a yfinance hiccup would block every BUY in the run. Blocking the whole book on a network blip is a worse failure than the fail-open it replaces, and the weekly universe review already bars sub-$1B names from entering. Enable only once per-proposal resolution is observed at ~100%.
book_risk._note: Book-level risk (added 2026-07-19 after an audit found every binding constraint was arithmetic on ONE proposal while portfolio_beta / shared_left_tail / corr_to_book were computed by tools/correlation.py and consumed only as prose). Four controls, all in tools/book_risk.py, all pure. (1) max_factor_stack_pct: aggregate notional across factor_map.AI_STACK_DRIVERS. The 2% per-driver risk cap permits ~2 positions per driver, so 8 positions across 4 AI-stack drivers was 100% AI exposure passing every existing limit - a per-driver cap is not a factor cap. (2) gap_adjusted_heat: the 8% heat cap sums (cost-stop)*qty, which assumes stops FILL AT THE STOP - contradicted by execution_costs.stop_gap_atr_fraction (0.5) in this same file, and by the only closed stop in the ledger (DELL plan stop 408.00, fill 389.75, 4.5% through, realized -13.5% on a position sized for 1%). Heat now adds the modelled gap-through, using correlation only to decide how much of the book gaps on the same morning - NEVER to hand budget back, since the plain sum is already the fully-correlated case. Unknown correlation assumes the worst. (3) max_portfolio_beta: MV-weighted against EQUITY not invested capital, so a half-cash book reads as half-exposed. (4) stress_scenarios: named shocks priced against the book the proposal WOULD create; losses deliberately NOT floored at stops, because a shock worth naming is one where stops gap. driver_shocks key __ai_stack__ shocks the whole factor group. All four fail CLOSED on unverifiable inputs, matching the portfolio_heat_unverifiable precedent.

learning_controls._note: Code-enforced Learning Protocol. Under min_trades_for_binding: no hard rejections from calibration_gate. At/above: high-conf inflation caps confidence; losing sector/theme buckets require calibration_exception text. Shadow book binds caution at 8 closed shadows (separate).
learning_controls._target_calibration_note: Added 2026-07-19. min_risk_reward_ratio (2.0) is the system's most rigorously justified rule - the config carries the expectancy math - and it is computed from the LLM's own target_price, which appears ZERO times in execution/exit_guard.py. Exits are stop, trail or horizon only; CLAUDE.md calls the target 'a milestone, not a tripwire'. So the gate filtered on a number nothing enforced or graded, and the model could always clear it by writing a bigger one. Targets stay NON-BINDING for exits (letting winners run is correct and literature-supported) - instead every close is graded on claimed RR vs REALIZED RR and target attainment. Binds only at min_trades_for_binding closed trades; at n=2 it reports phase 'anecdote' and withholds the binding-grade number entirely.

stop_engineering.note: ENFORCED stop floor per name. Your stop_loss must sit at least min_stop_distance_pct below entry or the validator rejects it (stop_inside_noise_band). position_stop_cushion.note: For each open position: room left between today's price and your recorded stop, measured in the name's own ATR. cushion_in_atr < 1 (inside_noise_band true) means one ordinary session could hit the stop - decide deliberately (hold through it, or exit on your terms) rather than get noise-stopped. The safety layer still enforces the recorded stop on a closing basis.

process_checklist.note: Required reasoning order every run. Work top-down; do not propose a BUY before completing the steps above it. Cite the relevant context-bundle blocks in commentary when a step changes your aggression.

steps.title: Macro regime check

steps.title: Portfolio / book review

steps.title: Idea selection
steps.must: From universe_scan / watchlist / tape promotions, pick at most a handful of candidates. Prefer fat pitches over marginal RR. Empty proposals with a clear no_trade_reason is a valid outcome.

steps.title: Entry geometry & underwrite
steps.must: For each candidate: charts, volume, stop/target geometry, fundamentals freshness, filings, catalysts. WebSearch mandatory before proposing a BUY. Variant perception required. Size and RR must clear validator floors as a MINIMUM, not a target.

steps.title: Kill conditions

recent.topic: Revenue-confirmed vs expense-driven beats: an EPS beat backed by a same-direction revenue surprise is the more persistent signal, so grade the SOURCE of the beat before treating a print gap as an epis
recent.summary: Ertimur, Livnat and Martikainen (2003, Review of Accounting Studies) show investors pay more for a dollar of revenue surprise than for a dollar of expense surprise at the preliminary earnings announcement, and that the gap varies with growth vs value status and cost structure. The mechanism, developed in Jegadeesh and Livnat (2006, Journal of Accounting and Economics), is persistence: earnings growth that comes from revenue tends to persist, while growth from cost cuts tends not to. Jegadeesh and Livnat find that after controlling for the earnings surprise, large revenue surprises predict abnormal returns over the following six months, strongest when revenue and earnings surprises point the same way, and that analysts also update too slowly on revenue surprises (forecast errors still linked to them 5 to 6 months later). The important caveat for this book: the six-month drift was significant for small firms but NOT for large firms. For large firms, the underreaction shows up mainly in the window around the NEXT earnings announcement, where returns are still related to the prior quarter's revenue surprise. Ertimur and Livnat (2002, Journal of Portfolio Management) add the sign logic: confirming positive sales and profit signals get a positive reaction, and a growth company that beats on profit while sales are flat or falling gets a negative reaction, while value companies are rewarded for that same cost control. Rees and Sivaramakrishnan (2007, Contemporary Accounting Research)
recent.how_to_apply: Before any episodic-pivot / earnings-gap entry under KB-3704904010, classify the print in the thesis: revenue_confirmed (revenue beat AND EPS beat, same direction), eps_only (EPS beat on inline or missed revenue, i.e. margin or cost driven), or revenue_only. Use the news headline or filing for revenue vs consensus, and quarterly_fundamentals revenue history for YoY acceleration as the time-series check; if the revenue line is not in context, write revenue_source unknown and do not treat it as confirmed. For a growth or AI-stack name, an eps_only beat should not take full size on a 0.60+ confidence; shade it to a probe or wait for the day-after hold to prove itself, and a gap built on a long-dated target with no reported revenue beat (like MRVL's investor-day gap, which filled within two days, n=1 anecdote) is graded as guidance under the pre-print and invalidator rules, not as a print. A revenue_confirmed beat is a legitimate input to the pre-print fork (KB-5731674677) in favor of holding a winner through the next report, since that is where large-cap underreaction to revenue shows up; it never overrides the 1% risk budget, the 2:1 RR floor, or the stop.

recent.topic: Re-entry after a stop-out: the stop is a verdict on that entry, not a ban on the ticker; re-buy only on a fresh named trigger (reclaim of the stopped level or a new base), never out of regret, revenge
recent.summary: Strahilevitz, Odean and Barber (Journal of Marketing Research, 2011), using trade records for 66,465 households (1991-96) and 665,533 retail investors (1997-99), found that investors are far more willing to repurchase stocks they previously sold for a gain than ones sold for a loss, and prefer to repurchase stocks that fell after the sale over ones that rose. They attribute both to naive reinforcement learning and counterfactual regret, and report that neither pattern improved returns. So the two instincts after a stop-out, 'that name burned me, never again' and 'I'll buy it back now that it's cheaper than where I sold', are both emotional, not edges. The Original Turtle Rules took the opposite, mechanical stance: under the alternative 'Whipsaw' stop (1/2 N stop, 1/2% risk), a stopped-out unit was re-entered if price returned to its original entry price, which produced more losses and a lower win rate but was reported to be more profitable; Eckhardt told the Turtles to trade as though they did not know their entry price, and they re-entered whenever the system gave a fresh signal after a loss. Kaminski and Lo (Journal of Financial Markets, 2014) show stops subtract expected return under a random walk and only add value when returns carry momentum or regime persistence, which is why a re-entry rule matters: a stop that is never followed by re-entry turns a momentum name's normal noise into a permanent exit. Re-underwrite from zero: fresh confidence, fresh stop under the shakeout or new swing low (KB-2454897375), fresh 2:1 math from the new entry, and run the pre-print fork (KB-5731674677, KB-0801985270) if earnings sits in the window. recent.topic: Scheduled macro prints (FOMC/CPI/jobs) as a swing-entry calendar: the announcement premium argues against 'wait until after the Fed', the pre-FOMC drift has decayed, and a macro date is an index-gap s
recent.summary: Savor and Wilson (2013, JFQA) found that average stock returns and Sharpe ratios are significantly higher on days with scheduled inflation, unemployment and FOMC announcements than on other days; the NBER macro announcement premium paper extends this to 1961-2023 and still finds it large and significant. Brusa, Savor and Wilson report a US FOMC-day excess return of about 24.8 bps versus about 1.3 bps on non-announcement days, while separately estimated CPI and jobs premia were positive but not statistically significant in their sample, i.e. the premium has migrated toward the FOMC. Lucca and Moench (2015) located the FOMC piece in the 24 hours BEFORE the 2pm statement (about 49 bps on average, 1994-2011, not reversed afterward, and zero on average from 2pm to the close). Kurov, Wolfe and Gilbert (2021) extended the sample to 2019 and found the pre-FOMC drift essentially disappeared after 2015, plausibly because uncertainty fell; a 2025 QuantSeeker backtest through 2024 claims it persists, mostly in high-VIX regimes, but its own commenters could not reproduce an edge, so treat the drift as weak and regime-dependent, not a timing signal. Cieslak, Morse and Vissing-Jorgensen (2019) found the 1994-2016 equity premium was earned in even weeks of the FOMC cycle, and a 2026 Federal Reserve FEDS paper notes that cycle turned negative in 2017-2021, so calendar-week patterns are fragile too. The durable, well-replicated part is narrow: scheduled macro risk is compensated on average rat
recent.how_to_apply: When a fat-pitch setup qualifies on its own rails (structure, RR >= 2:1, ATR-floored stop) and the only reason to wait is an upcoming FOMC statement, CPI or jobs print, do NOT write 'wait until after the Fed' as a skip or watch reason; the evidence says those days are compensated on average, and that reason feeds shadow-book regret_miss. Size it normally under the 1% risk budget and 8% heat cap; the macro date is an index-level gap input, so only shade size (e.g. half-risk probe) when the name is high beta (> ~1.8) or rate-sensitive AND the ATR stop sits within roughly one day's index move of price. Never open a position BECAUSE an FOMC is near (the pre-FOMC drift is decayed and regime-dependent), and never let a calendar-week pattern set entry timing. Keep earnings binaries on the separate expected-move rule (KB-0801985270 / KB-8308262054). For the current calendar, the next scheduled FOMC statement is Oct 28, 2026 (meeting Oct 27-28), one day before ILMN's 10/29 print; that FOMC date alone is not a reason to exit or defer, but the ILMN earnings binary still is.

tensions.why: That lesson sizes single-name earnings binaries against the options expected move; this one covers index-level scheduled macro prints, whose gap risk is smaller and compensated on average, so the earnings rule still governs prints and macro dates only shade size for high-beta, tight-stop names.

Breadth remains the regime aggression dial (a condition); this lesson only says a scheduled macro date by itself is not a reason to stand aside, so both apply: breadth sets aggression, the macro calendar is not a veto.

recent.topic: Price-contingent '≤ level' buy triggers carry two-sided adverse selection: they fill most on bad-news days and miss most on good-news days — pair every pullback level with a pre-committed strength pat
recent.summary: A 'buy at or below X' trigger (a resting limit or a would_buy_at level checked at slots) is price-contingent, and that contingency is not neutral. Handa & Schwartz (JF 1996) name the two risks: an adverse information event triggers an undesirable execution, and favorable news causes a desirable execution never to happen; on 1988 Dow-stock data they find limit-order returns conditional on NON-execution are lower, i.e. missing is a real cost, and limit orders only pay when temporary liquidity-driven dips (which revert) offset the information-driven ones (which do not). Linnainmaa (JF 2010, all Finnish individual investors plus simulations) shows the effect is large enough to mechanically manufacture apparent bad timing: limit buys execute after declines, sells after rises, and limit fills lose money when new information arrives — poor post-trade returns and 'contrarian' behaviour appear even without a behavioural bias. Harris & Hasbrouck (JFQA 1996, NYSE SuperDOT) is the honest counterweight: limit orders at or better than the quote beat market orders even after imputing a penalty for unexecuted orders, and they give separate measures for traders who MUST trade versus passive traders who can walk away — so patience is not wrong, it just has a measurable price. Perold (JPM 1988) supplies the accounting: implementation shortfall = execution cost on filled shares + opportunity cost on unfilled shares ((end price − decision price) × unfilled), so a level that never prints is not 'f
recent.how_to_apply: When a watchlist or thesis note writes a 'BUY ≤ $X' level, also write — at the same time — the strength path it will accept instead (e.g. a daily close above the inner pivot / prior high per KB-0246322924 and KB-9692173165), or state explicitly that it is pullback-only and will accept missing. When a ≤level trigger actually prints, do not treat the print as the licence: check the fill-day context in the bundle — if the name gapped down, carries fresh name-specific negative news, or the drop came on above-average volume, re-underwrite the thesis_invalidators before buying (this is the adverse-selection fill); if it is a quiet low-volume pullback to a named rail on a tape-wide dip, it is the fill the level was designed for (KB-6241168493). Grade the triggers Perold-style in aggregate: for unprinted levels use the shadow book's watchlist_hold regret_miss/good_skip as the opportunity-cost ledger, and only conclude a trigger family is too tight with n≥30 bar-verified verdicts — never widen one name's level after it ran (KB-8420105363). Nothing here changes stop placement, sizing, the 2:1 floor or the 10% upside bar.

tensions.why: The no-supply pullback entry remains the preferred fill; this lesson adds the fill-day test that separates a quiet liquidity dip to the rail (take it) from an information-driven drop through it (re-underwrite first).

The inner-pivot lesson already notes many breakouts never throw back; this lesson supplies the microstructure reason (favorable news prevents limit execution) and makes the paired strength trigger a decision-time requirement.

recent.topic: Stop underwriting: entry location is the binding lever; MAE is a path diagnostic — do not tighten from n=2
recent.summary: Two essays were one underwriting rule. A stop is a trigger that becomes a market order (Schwager/Schwab/SEC): fill is guaranteed, price is not, so 1R is a FLOOR on the loss, not a ceiling — DELL's 408 plan filled at 389.75 (0.55 ATR / 4.47% through → realized −1.43R). Kaminski & Lo (SIFR 63 / JFM 2014): under a random walk stops always reduce expected return and only pay when momentum is present; a stop inside the noise band is a tax. Noise scales with sqrt(t), and Danielsson & Zigrand (JBF 2006) show jumps make sqrt(t) understate risk at longer horizons — so min_stop_distance_pct is a ONE-DAY floor, not a multi-week band. Aim ~1.5–2×ATR beyond the named structural low (never past 15%); the free lever is ENTRY LOCATION (buy the pullback/throwback/day-after-gap-low so the same stop clears both the sqrt(t) band and a typical 0.5-ATR gap-through as a fraction of R), not stop width. John Sweeney's MAE/MFE (TASC 1985/1991; Campaign Trading; Maximum Adverse Excursion) measure the PATH, not the blotter: winner-MAE and loser-MAE separate when the entry has edge, and the stop belongs just beyond the winner cluster. Normalize in R or ATR and require 30–100 trades per setup before changing a stop — two closed trades are anecdotes (Tharp curve-fitting; LuxAlgo regime shift). Do NOT take the blog 'tighten to winner-MAE' half as a standing rule, and do NOT jump to breakeven at +0.5R/+1R (that guts 3–90d expectancy and fights the chandelier). Live MAE is already position_stop_cushion.cushio
recent.how_to_apply: Before any BUY, underwrite realized-R not planned-R. Place stop_loss beyond the named structural low AND at least stop_engineering.min_stop_distance_pct (aim 1.5–2×ATR, never past 15%) so one width clears both the sqrt(t) noise band until the nearest catalyst and a typical 0.5-ATR gap-through as a fraction of R. Prefer the low-MAE entries already in the playbooks (pullback / throwback / day-after-gap-low). Check 2:1 and 10% still clear after that floor; on event names demand ~2.5:1. Read cushion_in_atr as remaining room to 1R and as gap-exposure. Do NOT refit the entry stop from two closes, do NOT tighten toward a winner-MAE cliff, and do NOT move to breakeven at +1R — the 3×ATR chandelier (ratchet-only from high-water since entry) is the designed capture/exit overlay.

Chevron to Divest its Ownership Interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin Crude Midstream Assets
•Chevron to divest its ownership interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets in exchange for extended and improved Bakken midstream commercial terms
•Expected to improve Chevron’s Bakken cost structure and increase return on capital employed
•Supports competitive upstream development activity
HOUSTON, October 6, 2026 — Chevron Corporation (NYSE: CVX) announced today that several of its subsidiaries have entered into a series of definitive agreements with Hess Midstream LP (NYSE: HESM) to restructure the terms of its Bakken midstream contracts and establish new DJ Basin midstream contracts. The revised agreements extend the Bakken contracts and are expected to reduce Chevron's Bakken unit midstream costs by approximately 50%, enhancing future earnings and return on capital employed. In exchange for the improved long-term commercial framework and $200 million in cash consideration, Chevron will transfer to Hess Midstream its ownership interests and general partner position in Hess Midstream, as well as its DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets.
As part of this transaction, Chevron expects to fully deconsolidate Hess Midstream, including approximately $3.7 billion of Hess Midstream's debt. Chevron expects this transaction to be accretive to return on capital employed by 0.5% on an absolute basis and generate long-term future economic value through a lower cost structure and improved earnings. At closing, Chevron expects to recognize a one-time after-tax loss estimated at approximately $3 to $4 billion,1 given that the company is unable to recognize future Bakken midstream cost savings as an asset.
“This transaction resets the commercial framework between our upstream and midstream assets in the Bakken and DJ Basins,” said Andy Walz, Chevron’s President of Downstream, Midstream and Chemicals. “It lowers our Bakken cost structure while positioning Hess Midstream to advance as an independent company.” Chevron expects to sustain Bakken production through ongoing technology deployment and operational improvements drawn from its global shale and tight portfolio.
1 Expected to be treated as a special item.
Approvals and Timing
The transaction has been approved by the Conflicts Committee of the Board of Directors of the general partner of Hess Midstream, comprised entirely of independent directors, following consultation with its independent legal and financial advisors. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals and is expected to close by year-end 2026.
Advisors
BofA Securities is acting as financial advisor and Latham & Watkins LLP is acting as legal advisor to Chevron. Evercore is acting as financial advisor and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP is acting as legal advisor to the Conflicts Committee of the Board of Directors of the general partner of Hess Midstream.

Chevron is one of the world’s leading integrated energy companies. We believe affordable, reliable and ever-cleaner energy is essential to enabling human progress. Chevron produces crude oil and natural gas; manufactures transportation fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals and additives; and develops technologies that enhance our business and the industry. We aim to grow our oil and gas business, lower the carbon intensity of operations, and grow new energies businesses. More information about Chevron is available at www.chevron.com.

COST.label: Quality compounder / broad-market leader (default quality screen)
COST.weight: FCF, ROIC-style quality, growth durability, balance sheet, valuation vs history.

lines.why: Compounders buy back stock and fund growth from ops.
lines.good_looks_like: Consistent positive FCF; FCF margin healthy.
lines.red_flag: FCF collapse or chronic miss.

lines.why: Need growth to support the multiple.
lines.good_looks_like: Steady mid-to-high single digit or better with stability.
lines.red_flag: Stagnation at a growth multiple.

lines.why: Net debt / leverage must be sane.
lines.good_looks_like: Net cash or modest net debt / EBITDA.
lines.red_flag: Leverage spike without earnings power.

lines.why: Moat shows up in margins.
lines.good_looks_like: Stable/expanding.
lines.red_flag: Structural margin decay.

lines.why: Quality is not always cheap.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs growth and history.
lines.red_flag: Top-decile multiple with slowing growth.

lines.why: Revisions drive near-term swings.
lines.good_looks_like: Flat to up.
lines.red_flag: Cuts into elevated expectations.

COST.note: Answer each line briefly before a BUY. Model-specific: do not force SaaS FCF rules on capex-growth names, or ignore FCF on mature compounders.

CVX.label: Energy / power generation / equipment
CVX.weight: Commodity or load outlook, spark spreads, backlog, balance sheet.

lines.why: Cash flows track power prices / utilization / data-center load.
lines.good_looks_like: Supportive curves or contracted offtake.
lines.red_flag: Collapsing prices with high fixed costs.

lines.why: Equipment names live on orders.
lines.good_looks_like: Backlog multi-year; book-to-bill >1.
lines.red_flag: Order cliff.

lines.why: Cyclical cash flows + debt is dangerous.
lines.good_looks_like: Deleveraging, positive FCF at mid-cycle.
lines.red_flag: Peak leverage at peak prices.

lines.why: Street embeds commodity views.
lines.good_looks_like: Revisions stable/up.
lines.red_flag: Cuts with no cycle bottom signal.

CVX.note: Answer each line briefly before a BUY. Model-specific: do not force SaaS FCF rules on capex-growth names, or ignore FCF on mature compounders.

NOW.label: Software / SaaS / platforms (subscription, high incremental margin)
NOW.weight: Growth + retention + FCF conversion + rule-of-40 style quality.

lines.why: SaaS value is durable growth and expansion.

lines.red_flag: Neither growth nor FCF working.

lines.why: Multiple compression follows estimate cuts.

NTAP.label: Capex-growth / AI capacity scale-up (neocloud, infra buildout)
NTAP.weight: Revenue growth, estimate *direction*, liquidity, utilization narrative — NOT near-term FCF vs SaaS peers.

lines.why: Scale-ups are judged on whether demand is real and accelerating.
lines.good_looks_like: High / sustained revenue growth; fwd growth still elevated; revisions stable or up.
lines.red_flag: Growth decelerating hard while the multiple still prices perfection; large negative EPS revisions.

lines.why: Negative FCF is normal only if the balance sheet can fund the build.
lines.good_looks_like: Large cash, manageable net debt, access to capital, current ratio healthy.
lines.red_flag: Cash burn path that exhausts runway without clear funding; covenant / refinance stress.

lines.why: FCF will look 'bad' during build — ask if capex is productive capacity.
lines.good_looks_like: Capex tied to capacity customers will rent; management frames path to utilization.
lines.red_flag: Capex without demand visibility; FCF worsening while growth also stalls.

lines.why: Hyperscalers and custom silicon can reprice the entire model.
lines.good_looks_like: Sticky customers, differentiated capacity, pricing not in free-fall.
lines.red_flag: Price wars, TPU/ASIC displacement narrative with no rebuttal.

lines.why: Street estimates are the near-term scoreboard for a 3–90d swing.
lines.good_looks_like: EPS/revenue revisions flat to up over 30d.
lines.red_flag: Sharp downward revisions into a rich multiple.

ASML.label: Semiconductor / hardware cyclical (memory, foundry-sensitive, equipment)
ASML.weight: Cycle position and inventory > headline P/E. Low fwd multiples at peak earnings are often traps.

lines.why: Cheap fwd P/E on peak EPS is not value.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs mid-cycle earnings power, not peak.
lines.red_flag: Thesis is only 'cheapest in group' without cycle underwriting.

lines.why: GPU/hyperscaler buyers dominate some nodes.
lines.good_looks_like: Diversified end demand or multi-year capacity contracts.
lines.red_flag: One customer can cancel the cycle.

lines.why: Revisions lead the cycle more than price alone.
lines.good_looks_like: Revisions up or stabilizing after a washout.
lines.red_flag: Revisions still rolling over into a bounce.
